# System sub-actions

## Get clipboard text

Reads the text you last copied (Ctrl+C) and saves it in a variable. Handy for turning a copied link into a chat message.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Save in variable** | The variable that receives the copied text, without % signs. The default clipboardText means you use %clipboardText%. Starts as: `clipboardText`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%clipboardText%` | The copied text (the variable name can be changed in the settings) |
| `%clipboardTextFound%` | True if there was text on the clipboard |

<small>Type id: `desktop.getClipboard`</small>

## Keyboard press

Presses keys on your keyboard for you, as if you typed them, in whatever program is in front. Good for triggering another program's shortcut.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Keys** | A shortcut like "Ctrl+Shift+F1". For several in a row, separate them with commas, like "Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V". On Linux the desktop may ask for permission once. Starts as: `Ctrl+Shift+F1`. |
| **Pause between combos (ms)** | How many milliseconds to wait between shortcuts when you list several. 1000 = 1 second. Starts as: `30`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%keysPressed%` | The shortcuts that were pressed |

<small>Type id: `input.keyboardPress`</small>

## Run program

Starts a program or opens a file on your computer, like a script or another tool. It can wait until the program ends and even collect what it prints.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Program or file** | The program or file to open, with its full location, like C:\Tools\clip.exe or /usr/bin/notify-send. |
| **Command-line options** | Extra words to give the program, like "--fast". Empty is fine for most programs. |
| **Working directory** | The folder the program starts in. Empty = the default. Most people can leave this alone. |
| **Wait for exit** | Tick to wait for the program to finish before the next step. Unticked, Cuebot goes on straight away. Starts as: `false`. |
| **Wait at most (seconds, 0 = no limit)** | With "Wait for exit": give up waiting after this many seconds. 0 = wait as long as it takes. Starts as: `0`. |
| **Capture output (%output1%...)** | Tick to save the lines the program prints in %output1%, %output2% and so on. Only works together with "Wait for exit". Starts as: `false`. |
| **Environment variables** | Extra settings for the program, one per line as NAME=value. Most people leave this empty. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%exitCode%` | The number the program ended with (0 usually means it went fine). Only after waiting. |
| `%timedOut%` | True if you stopped waiting because the time ran out. Only after waiting. |
| `%output1%` | The first line the program printed (output2 is the second). Only with capture output. |
| `%outputCount%` | How many lines the program printed. Only with capture output. |

<small>Type id: `core.runProgram`</small>

## Set clipboard text

Puts text on your clipboard, so you can paste it with Ctrl+V. Handy to copy a link or a viewer's message.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Text** | The text to copy. You can use %variables%, like %message%. |

<small>Type id: `desktop.setClipboard`</small>

## Set watcher state

Turns a watcher or a followed file on, off or flips it. Watchers are made on the Watchers page. Turn one off if you do not need it right now.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Watcher or file tail** | The name of the watcher or followed file, exactly as on the Watchers page. |
| **State** | Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite. Options: Enable, Disable, Toggle. Starts as: `Enable`. |

<small>Type id: `core.setWatcherState`</small>

## Show desktop notification

Shows a small pop-up message on your computer screen, only for you, not your viewers. Good as a private reminder. Click it to start an action with the "Toast notification clicked" trigger.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **Title** | The bold line at the top of the pop-up. The default is Cuebot. Starts as: `Cuebot`. |
| **Message** | The text of the pop-up. You can use %variables%. |
| **Icon file** | Optional. The location of a small picture file to show next to the text. |
| **Notification id** | Optional. A name you make up so the "Toast notification clicked" trigger can tell which pop-up was clicked. |
| **Seconds on screen** | How many seconds the pop-up stays on screen. From 1 to 120. Starts as: `5`. |
| **Show with** | Auto = your system's notifications where possible, else Cuebot's own pop-up. In-app = always Cuebot's own. System = your system's. Options: Auto, In-app, System. Starts as: `Auto`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%notificationShownWith%` | Which way the pop-up was shown |

<small>Type id: `desktop.showNotification`</small>
